title: Apply as Careworker
feature_summary: This public application form is where a person providing support begins. It collects the information needed for organizational review and later matching, without requiring an account first.

title: Home
feature_summary: The public landing page introduces CareWeb AI as a coordination and matching workspace for people receiving support, careworkers, and organizations.

title: Login
feature_summary: The login screen is the entry point for role-specific dashboards. CareWeb AI uses the signed-in user's role and organization membership to show the appropriate tools.

title: Careworker Dashboard
feature_summary: The careworker dashboard summarizes active relationships, schedules, pending actions, and links to the careworker's profile and matching tools.

title: Careworker Profile
feature_summary: The profile presents the information used for compatibility: experience, location, availability, languages, transportation, preferences, and notes. The careworker can review and update these sections.

title: Tag Matching — Find Clients
purpose: Filter possible clients by care criteria
feature_summary: The careworker selects one or more care tags and uses Find Clients. Results show the relevant client, compatibility information, overlapping tags, and the option to request a match.

title: AI Matching — Careworker
feature_summary: The AI Match action evaluates the careworker's profile and selected criteria to rank potential clients and explain the score. It supports the careworker's review and choice rather than automatically creating a relationship.

title: Schedule Detail
feature_summary: The schedule detail page shows the client, careworker, organization, dates, recurring time slots, approvals, notes, and response status for the working relationship.

title: Rate Your Experience
feature_summary: After a session, the careworker can independently rate care fit, communication, reliability, and workload balance on a 1–10 scale. These ratings contribute to human-reviewed stability insights.

title: Login
feature_summary: Staff sign in to access organization-level rosters, approvals, matching tools, schedules, and relationship-support indicators.

title: Organization Dashboard
feature_summary: The staff dashboard provides a consolidated view of participants, active matches, schedules, and Stability Snapshot status so staff can prioritize follow-up.

title: Careworker Pool
feature_summary: The careworker pool lets staff review participating careworkers, their approval status, and profile information used for safe and relevant matching.

title: Client Pool
feature_summary: The client pool gives staff a separate view of client applications, review status, and profile links so the organization can coordinate participation and matching.

title: Tag Matching — Staff
feature_summary: Staff can choose a direction, select a careworker or client, apply tags, and use Find Matches. This is a transparent criteria-based workflow before considering AI assistance.

title: AI Matching — Staff
feature_summary: The staff AI matching page accepts optional careworker/client constraints and tags, then presents scores, matched tags, AI reasoning, and a human-controlled Propose Match action.

title: Stability Snapshot — Stable
feature_summary: This populated example shows the Green/Stable relationship state, overall score, five relationship signals, glossary definitions, and the underlying client/careworker session ratings.

title: Stability Snapshot — At Risk
feature_summary: This second seeded client/careworker match demonstrates the Red/At Risk state and shows how low or concerning rating patterns are made visible for staff support conversations.

title: Flag for Stabilization Review
feature_summary: Staff can flag the at-risk relationship directly from the real Stability Detail control. The resulting state records that review is requested and changes the Support Flags signal to Immediate review recommended.

title: Flagged for Stabilization Review
feature_summary: After staff submits the real flag action, the page confirms the relationship is flagged, identifies the request, and shows the updated Support Flags signal.

title: Apply for Support
feature_summary: This public application form is where a person looking for support begins. It collects care needs and personal context for organizational review and later matching.

title: Home
feature_summary: The landing page explains the purpose of the registry and provides clear paths for people seeking support, careworkers, and organizations.

title: Login
feature_summary: The client signs in to see their own care coordination workspace and information, separate from staff and careworker views.

title: Client Dashboard
feature_summary: The client dashboard summarizes matches, schedules, approvals, session information, and invitations for a support person or coordinator.

title: Client Profile
feature_summary: The client profile captures care needs, programs, availability, languages, scheduling preferences, and other context so matching can reflect the client's circumstances.

title: Tag Matching — Find Careworkers
feature_summary: The client selects one or more care-needs tags and uses Find Careworkers. Results show potential careworkers, matched criteria, explanations, and a client-controlled Request Match action.

title: AI Matching — Client
feature_summary: The AI Match action ranks careworkers against the client's needs, availability, and selected tags, and displays reasoning so the client can make an informed choice.

title: Schedule Detail
feature_summary: The client can review recurring time slots, approval state, participating careworker, notes, and session-level actions in one place.

title: Rate Your Experience
feature_summary: The client uses the same independent rating categories to describe care fit, communication, reliability, and workload balance. Both perspectives help staff identify patterns without replacing human judgment.
